blocks.prompt: 10 Solve the following trigonometric equation: \(\cos 2x = \cos x\)
blocks.explanation:
Different angles again; the right side has \(\cos x\), so use the form \(\cos 2x = 2\cos^{2}x - 1\) that contains only cosine.
This gives a quadratic in \(\cos x\).
Plan: factorise, solve \(\cos x = 1\) and \(\cos x = -\frac{1}{2}\).
steps:
Given: \(\cos 2x = \cos x\).
To find: principal solutions and general solution.
Method: \(\cos 2x = 2\cos^{2}x - 1\), then solve the quadratic in \(\cos x\).

Use the double-angle formula
\[2\cos^{2}x - 1 = \cos x\]
\[2\cos^{2}x - \cos x - 1 = 0\]
Why: of the three forms of \(\cos 2x\), this one contains only \(\cos x\), like the right side.

Factorise
\[2\cos^{2}x - 2\cos x + \cos x - 1 = 0\]
\[2\cos x(\cos x - 1) + 1(\cos x - 1) = 0\]
\[(2\cos x + 1)(\cos x - 1) = 0\]
Why: product \(2 \times (-1) = -2\), sum \(-1\): the numbers are \(-2\) and \(+1\).

Two basic equations
\[\cos x = -\dfrac{1}{2}\ \text{ or }\ \cos x = 1\]
Why: each factor is set to zero.

When \(\cos x = 1\)
\[x = 0,\ 2\pi\]
in \([0, 2\pi]\); in general \(x = 2n\pi\).
Why: cosine is 1 only at the starting point of the circle.

When \(\cos x = -\frac{1}{2}\)
Cosine is negative: quadrants II and III, reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\).
\[x = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\]
\[x = \pi + \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\]
Why: \(\cos\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2}\).

General solution
\[\left\{2n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{2\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{4\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\right\},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\]
Why: the period of \(\cos x\) is \(2\pi\). (The three families are equally spaced, \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) apart, so they can also be written as \(x = \frac{2n\pi}{3}\).)

Check
\[x = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}:\ \cos\dfrac{4\pi}{3} = -\dfrac{1}{2} = \cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\]
\[x = 0:\ \cos 0 = 1 = \cos 0\]
Why: both sides are equal; \(\frac{4\pi}{3}\) works the same way since \(\cos\frac{8\pi}{3} = \cos\frac{2\pi}{3} = -\frac{1}{2}\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: The textbook prints no answers for Exercise 10.1. Every answer on this page is ours: worked out step by step, checked independently with a computer algebra system (sympy) and compared with a solution book. As in the book's examples, we give the principal solutions in \([0, 2\pi]\) and the general solution as a union of sets.
